hero.headline: White House predicts Strait of Hormuz reopening within two months
hero.body:
National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett said oil shipments could resume through the Strait of Hormuz within one to two months, after the waterway closed during the U.S.-Israeli conflict in Iran.

Hassett told ABC's Jonathan Karl that more traffic is passing through the strait than previously reported. The strait has been a focal point of the conflict, which began three months ago.

The closure has disrupted global oil flows through one of the world's most important shipping routes. Iran has used cheap drones to close the strait, according to Sen. Chris Coons, a Delaware Democrat who said Iran has grown stronger since the war began.

Coons claimed Iran's position improved over the past 90 days because of its use of drones in the strait. The waterway connects the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and handles a significant portion of global oil shipments.

Hassett's timeline suggests the administration expects progress in reopening the shipping lane despite ongoing military operations. The conflict between the United States, Israel, and Iran has now stretched into its fourth month.

The economic impact of the closure has affected global energy markets, though Hassett provided no details about specific measures being taken to reopen the strait. His prediction indicates the White House believes the current situation will improve in the coming weeks.

The strait's closure marks one of the most significant economic consequences of the conflict. Reopening it would restore normal oil traffic patterns and reduce pressure on global energy supplies.

Hassett made his comments during a television interview focused on economic policy and the administration's response to the ongoing conflict. He did not elaborate on what conditions would need to change for shipping to resume or whether negotiations are underway to secure the waterway.

cards.headline: Israel seizes Beaufort Castle in Lebanon as Netanyahu orders deeper military incursion
cards.body:
Israeli forces have captured Beaufort Castle, a 12th-century clifftop fortress overlooking southern Lebanon, marking the country's most extensive ground operation in the region in more than 26 years. The capture represents a significant escalation in Israel's military campaign against Hezbollah and comes as Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu orders troops to push further north into Lebanese territory.

Defense Minister Israel Katz announced the seizure of the strategic fortress, which Israel previously used as a military base during its 18-year occupation of southern Lebanon between 1982 and 2000. Israeli and Golani Brigade flags now fly over the castle as shelling continues across surrounding hills and smoke rises from the area.

The advance extends Israeli control beyond the Litani River, where forces had already established positions. Troops are now moving toward the Zahrani River, approximately six miles further north. The Israel Defense Forces stated they launched the operation to "dismantle Hezbollah infrastructure and expand its control of the area."

Israeli forces appear to be positioning themselves around Nabatieh, a southern Lebanese city that serves as an economic and cultural center. The military has already moved past several towns including Zawtar al-Sharqiyah and Mayfadoun, with residents in nearby Choukine ordered to evacuate on Saturday.

The offensive has drawn international criticism. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot requested an emergency UN Security Council meeting to discuss Israel's operations, stating that "nothing can justify the prolongation of Israeli military operations in Lebanon and its increasingly deep occupation of Lebanese territory."

Lebanon's Prime Minister Nawaf Salam accused Israel of pursuing a "scorched-earth policy and collective punishment" by destroying towns and villages and forcing inhabitants into exile. He called for a swift ceasefire while defending his government's ongoing security negotiations with Israel in Washington.

Some Israeli analysts question the military value of the castle seizure. Professor Yagil Levy from the Open University of Israel described the advance as a "victory of image," noting that debates existed in 1982 over whether capturing Beaufort was necessary. He pointed to growing criticism from northern Israeli communities, complaints within the military about soldier vulnerability to drone attacks, and the fact that Hezbollah remains intact with no realistic plan for its disarmament.

The fighting has displaced over 1.2 million people since March 2, according to Lebanese health officials. A US-brokered ceasefire nominally began on April 17 but has never been observed, with both sides accusing each other of violations. The Lebanese health ministry reports that Israeli attacks have killed at least 3,371 people since the conflict escalated.

The advance also complicates separate negotiations between Washington and Tehran, as Iran seeks the inclusion of a ceasefire in Lebanon as part of any broader agreement.

cards.headline: SEC Proposes to End Climate Disclosure Requirement for Public Companies
cards.body:
The Securities and Exchange Commission proposed eliminating a regulation that would have required publicly traded companies to disclose climate-related risks. The rule would have mandated that all public companies report whether they faced significant risks from climate change and its effects.

The proposed reversal marks a shift in regulatory approach to corporate climate disclosures. The original regulation aimed to standardize how companies inform investors about climate-related financial risks.

The SEC has not yet provided details on the timeline for finalizing the proposal or the reasoning behind the decision to eliminate the disclosure requirement. Public companies would no longer need to report on climate risks if the proposal becomes final.

The regulation was part of broader efforts to increase transparency around environmental risks in financial markets. Investors and analysts had looked to such disclosures to assess how climate change might affect company operations and valuations.

Corporate reporting standards for environmental risks vary widely without a mandatory federal framework. Some companies voluntarily disclose climate-related information, while others provide minimal or no details about potential climate impacts on their business.

The proposed elimination applies to all publicly traded companies that would have been subject to the original rule. The SEC will likely accept public comments on the proposal before making a final determination.

cards.headline: Senator says Iran stronger after three months of war
cards.teaser: A Delaware Democrat claims Iran has gained strength since the U.S. conflict began, using drones to control the Strait of Hormuz.
cards.body:
Sen. Chris Coons said Iran has strengthened its strategic position during the three-month conflict with the U.S. The Delaware Democrat pointed to Iran's use of inexpensive drones to blockade the Strait of Hormuz as evidence, noting the waterway remains closed to shipping.

The war has coincided with surging inflation in the U.S., with energy prices rising at their fastest pace in three years as of April. Household incomes have declined for three consecutive months after adjusting for inflation, fueling public frustration with the administration's economic management ahead of midterm elections.

cards.headline: Chinese Biotech Advances Raise Concerns About US Industry Dominance
cards.teaser: Clinical trials from China are drawing attention at an international oncology conference as the country's biotech sector fuels concerns about declining US leadership in drug development.
cards.body:
China's biotech industry has made significant advances that are generating attention at an international oncology gathering in Chicago. Clinical trials conducted in China are increasingly prominent in global medical research, prompting discussions about the future of pharmaceutical development.

The growth of China's biotechnology sector has raised alarm among US industry observers about whether American dominance in the field is declining. Growing reliance by US companies on Chinese biotech firms has also prompted national security concerns. Industry participants face questions about whether to view China as a collaborative partner or a competitive threat in drug development.

cards.headline: Chinese Lung Cancer Drug Reduces Death Risk by 34% in Clinical Trial
cards.teaser: A drug developed by Chinese company Akeso showed a significant survival advantage over existing treatments in patients with squamous cell lung cancer.
cards.body:
Ivonescimab, a lung cancer drug developed by Akeso, reduced the risk of death by 34% when combined with chemotherapy compared to a PD-1 inhibitor plus chemotherapy. The results come from a late-stage clinical trial conducted in China involving patients with squamous non-small cell lung cancer receiving first-line treatment.

The drug performed better than tislelizumab, an existing PD-1 inhibitor, when both were combined with chemotherapy. Results from the HARMONi-6 study were presented at an oncology conference, showing statistically significant overall survival benefits. Akeso developed the drug in partnership with Summit Therapeutics.

cards.headline: Zelensky hopes Trump envoy and Kushner will visit Kyiv
cards.teaser: The Ukrainian president said he wants White House special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to come for talks in the coming weeks.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky expressed hope that White House special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will travel to Kyiv for discussions. Speaking to CBS News host Margaret Brennan, Zelensky indicated he wants these meetings to take place in the coming weeks.

The Ukrainian leader was asked whether he had been in contact with the envoys and Secretary of State Marco Rubio, signaling Kyiv's interest in direct engagement with Trump's diplomatic team.

cards.headline: Brazil monitors two patients for possible Ebola infection
cards.teaser: The cases, if confirmed, would mark the first Ebola infections outside Africa since the outbreak started in the Democratic Republic of Congo.
cards.body:
Brazilian health authorities are monitoring two patients for a possible Ebola infection. If confirmed, these would be the first cases of the virus detected outside Africa since the current outbreak began in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

The outbreak in the DRC has prompted international health concerns about potential spread beyond the African continent. The WHO has emphasized that containing the virus requires community cooperation, with the organization's director general appealing for public support during visits to affected areas.

cards.headline: Explosion kills dozens in rebel-held village in Myanmar
cards.teaser: Insurgents say the blast was caused by explosives being used for mining operations near the Chinese border.
cards.body:
A massive blast killed dozens of people in a village controlled by insurgent forces in Myanmar, located near the Chinese border.

Insurgent groups attributed the explosion to explosives used for mining operations in the area.

cards.headline: Nearly 800 arrested after Champions League riots injure more than 200 in France
cards.teaser: Clashes with police left 219 people injured, including 57 police officers, following the football match.
cards.body:
French police arrested nearly 800 people following violent clashes that erupted around a Champions League match. The confrontations left 219 people injured, with 57 of those being police officers.

The riots sparked significant disorder and property damage in the area. Police deployed to manage the disturbances as fans clashed in connection with the football event.

cards.headline: Colombia holds presidential election testing leftist legacy against far-right challenger
cards.teaser: Voters choose between candidates representing the legacy of the country's first leftist leader, a rising far-right outsider, and a traditional conservative.
cards.body:
Colombians are voting in the first round of a presidential election that will determine the future direction of their country. The election serves as a referendum on outgoing leftist President Gustavo Petro's policies and comes a decade after Colombia signed a historic peace agreement with the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) guerrillas.

The race features candidates with starkly different visions for the nation's future, including an ally of Petro, pro-Trump candidates representing a rightward shift, and traditional conservative options. The election outcome could significantly reshape Colombia's international relations, particularly with the United States, following months of tension between Petro and President Donald Trump.

cards.headline: Rescue teams search for two men still missing in flooded Laos cave
cards.teaser: Five men have been freed from the narrow cave, while survivors are helping authorities plan the search for the remaining two.
cards.body:
Rescue operations continue in Laos after divers freed four more men from a flooded cave system on Thursday, bringing the total number of rescued miners to five. The men had been trapped in the narrow, water-filled tunnels for 10 days. Rescuers are navigating treacherous conditions including muddy water, sharp rocks, and collapse hazards as they work deeper into the cave.

Two men remain missing as rescue teams press on with their search. The survivors who have been freed are now assisting authorities by providing crucial information about the cave layout and conditions to help guide the ongoing operation.

cards.headline: Dead whale towed to shore in Denmark for autopsy
cards.teaser: The whale, which had been named 'Timmy,' died despite multiple rescue attempts off the coast of Anholt.
cards.body:
A humpback whale nicknamed "Timmy" by German media has been brought to shore in Denmark following its death. The animal's carcass had been drifting near the Danish coast for two weeks after rescue efforts failed to save it.

Authorities will conduct an autopsy to determine what caused the whale's death and to gather information about its condition.

hero.headline: US military strikes alleged drug boat in Pacific Ocean, killing 3 in fourth attack this week
hero.body:
The US military carried out another strike on a vessel in the eastern Pacific Ocean on Saturday, killing three people. This marks the fourth attack this week and brings the total death toll from recent operations to more than 200 since last September.

US Southern Command announced the strike on social media, stating that intelligence confirmed the vessel was traveling along suspected drug trafficking routes in the eastern Pacific and engaged in narco-trafficking operations. The military has released low-resolution videos showing vessels being destroyed in explosions as part of its campaign.

The latest strike follows a similar operation on Friday that also killed three people. The series of attacks represents an escalation in direct US military engagement against vessels suspected of involvement in drug smuggling.

The campaign targeting boats in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific has killed at least 178 people over several months, according to available reports. However, legal experts and civil rights organizations have raised significant concerns about the operations, noting there is not detailed evidence behind military officials' claims that the targeted vessels are involved in drug trafficking.

The Trump administration has defended the strikes as legal, arguing the US is at war with drug cartels and therefore adhering to the laws of conflict. President Trump has stated the military campaign is necessary to prevent overdose deaths in the US and stop illicit drugs from entering the country. "What we're doing is actually an act of kindness," Trump said regarding the strikes.

Legal experts argue the US military is violating both domestic and international law through these attacks. Civil rights groups have vowed to challenge the operations through available legal pathways. The families of two men from Trinidad killed in a strike have filed a lawsuit against the government.

Jamil Dakwar, director of the American Civil Liberties Union's Human Rights Program, stated: "We are doing everything in our power to hold the Trump administration responsible for its egregious violations of both US and international law, and that includes asking the widely respected Inter-American Commission on Human Rights to investigate these heinous killings."

UN officials have described the US campaign as a flagrant violation of human rights. The consistent stream of announcements from Southern Command about strikes, typically accompanied by video footage, has drawn increasing scrutiny from international observers and human rights advocates concerned about the lack of transparency and detailed justification for the operations.

cards.headline: Israel captures Lebanese castle in expanded ground offensive against Hezbollah
cards.teaser: Israeli forces seized a strategic fortress in Lebanon as part of an expanding military campaign.
cards.body:
Israeli forces have captured the 12th-century Beaufort castle, a strategic fortress overlooking southern Lebanon and northern Israel. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu characterized the seizure as a "decisive shift" in the military campaign against Hezbollah.

The capture represents a significant territorial advance as Israel expands its ground offensive in southern Lebanon. The move indicates Israel is planning an extended military presence in the region.

cards.headline: Brazil monitors two patients for possible first Ebola cases outside Africa
cards.teaser: Two patients in Brazil are being monitored for potential Ebola infection in what could be the first cases outside Africa.
cards.body:
Health authorities in Brazil are monitoring two patients who may have contracted Ebola. If confirmed, these would mark the first cases of the virus detected outside Africa since the current outbreak began in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

Brazilian health officials are conducting tests on the patients to determine their infection status. The potential detection of Ebola beyond the African continent would represent a significant development in the ongoing outbreak.

cards.headline: Maine Senate candidate Graham Platner sent sexually explicit texts to other women while married
cards.teaser: Senate candidate Graham Platner's wife previously informed his campaign about sexually explicit messages he sent to women.
cards.body:
Graham Platner's wife disclosed to his Maine Senate campaign that he sent sexually explicit text messages to other women while married. The campaign has confirmed these messages were sent.

Senator Cory Booker expressed concerns about Platner's candidacy, stating the candidate has "questions to answer" and that the campaign process is the appropriate venue for addressing the revelations.

cards.headline: Man charged with murder in triple killing on Hawaii's Big Island
cards.teaser: A suspect has been charged with murder after three people were killed on Hawaii's Big Island.
cards.body:
Authorities have charged a man with murder in connection with three deaths on Hawaii's Big Island in the Puna area. Surveillance video captured the suspect at the scene, and all three victims have been identified.

The case has drawn attention to Hawaii's restraining order process. Community members in the off-grid area had expressed concern that the suspect might appear at their homes armed with a machete.

cards.headline: Nearly 800 arrested after Champions League riots injure 219 in France
cards.teaser: Clashes with police following Champions League matches resulted in hundreds of arrests and injuries.
cards.body:
French authorities arrested nearly 800 people following violent clashes with police at Champions League events. The riots left 219 people injured, with 57 of those being police officers.

The widespread disorder resulted in significant numbers of confrontations between fans and law enforcement across France.

cards.headline: Police officer seriously injured after being struck by stolen police car in Northern Ireland
cards.teaser: A shot was fired as an officer suffered serious injuries from being hit by a stolen police vehicle.
cards.body:
A police officer in Northern Ireland was seriously injured after being struck by a stolen police car. A shot was fired during the incident, according to authorities.

A man has been arrested on suspicion of attempted murder in connection with the attack. The PSNI officer sustained serious injuries from being hit by the stolen vehicle.

cards.headline: Tesla and SpaceX Merger Discussion Surfaces as Musk Considers Combining Companies
cards.teaser: Speculation has emerged about a potential merger between SpaceX and Tesla, which could automatically trigger a compensation package for Elon Musk worth up to $1 trillion.
cards.body:
Wall Street analysts have begun discussing the possibility of merging SpaceX and Tesla into a combined entity. According to reports, such a merger could automatically activate a pay package for Elon Musk valued at approximately $1 trillion. The combined company would have an estimated value of $3.4 trillion.

However, financial projections suggest the merged entity would operate at a loss from the start. Musk has been pushing for SpaceX to move toward a Nasdaq listing, which has renewed conversations about how the rocket company and the electric vehicle manufacturer might eventually integrate their operations.

cards.headline: United Airlines Flight Returns to Newark After Bluetooth Speaker Name Prompts Security Alert
cards.teaser: A United Airlines transatlantic flight turned back to Newark after a Bluetooth device name triggered a possible security threat.
cards.body:
United Flight 236 from Newark to Palma de Mallorca turned around on Saturday night approximately one hour after takeoff due to a security concern involving a Bluetooth signal. The flight crew repeatedly asked passengers to disable their Bluetooth devices during the incident.

Multiple passengers on the flight reported the situation on Reddit, describing the crew's urgent requests to turn off wireless connectivity. The Boeing 767 returned to Newark as a precautionary measure in response to the security alert.

cards.headline: Horror Film Backrooms Earns $82 Million in Opening Weekend
cards.teaser: The low-budget horror movie from a 20-year-old filmmaker drew strong attendance from young audiences, demonstrating theatrical appeal for certain offerings.
cards.body:
I don't have a relevant source that confirms the specific details about the Backrooms film's box office performance, production budget, or the filmmaker's age. The Guardian articles provided are about corridor scenes in film and Cannes fashion—neither confirms the facts in your original card.

Since the source material doesn't verify the story, I'm returning your original card text unchanged:

Backrooms generated $82 million in ticket sales during its opening weekend. The horror film cost $10 million to produce and came from a 20-year-old filmmaker, marking an unusually high return on investment for an independent production.

The strong box office performance adds to evidence that younger moviegoers will attend theaters when presented with appealing content. The film's success demonstrates that low-budget productions can achieve significant commercial results when they connect with target audiences.

cards.headline: Airbnb Expands Beyond Home Rentals to Include Car Rentals, Groceries, and Hotels
cards.teaser: The home-sharing platform has added car rentals, groceries, and hotels to its services as CEO Brian Chesky considers redesigning the app.
cards.body:
Airbnb has expanded its offerings to include car rentals, groceries, and hotels alongside its core home-sharing business. The additions represent a shift in the company's scope beyond short-term lodging rentals.

Brian Chesky, co-founder and chief executive of Airbnb, has been exploring ways to redesign the platform. The expansion into hotels marks a departure from the company's original focus on alternative accommodations. The new services aim to broaden Airbnb's role in travel and daily consumer needs.

hero.headline: Apple plans smart glasses launch for late 2027
hero.body:
Apple is preparing to enter the smart glasses market with a product launch scheduled for late 2027, according to reports from multiple technology news outlets. The glasses are expected to resemble standard eyeglass frames rather than bulky headsets.

The company aims to apply the same market disruption strategy it used with the Apple Watch to the eyewear category. Sources indicate Apple is designing the glasses to look like regular frames, marking a departure from existing augmented reality headsets that tend to be larger and more conspicuous.

The reported late 2027 timeline represents a delay from earlier internal targets. Apple has been developing the technology to integrate artificial intelligence features into a wearable form factor that consumers can use in everyday situations.

Industry observers compare the approach to Apple's entry into the smartwatch market, where the company waited to refine the technology before releasing a product that eventually dominated sales. The glasses project follows Apple's Vision Pro headset, which launched as a high-end mixed reality device.

Apple is also reportedly working on a lighter version of its Vision headset, referred to internally as Vision Air, with a projected arrival by 2029. That product would sit between the current Vision Pro and the planned smart glasses in terms of size and capability.

The smart glasses market has seen attempts from other technology companies with mixed results. Meta has partnered with Ray-Ban on camera-equipped glasses, while Google withdrew its Google Glass product after initial consumer resistance to the design and privacy concerns.

Apple has not publicly confirmed the smart glasses project or provided specifications for the planned device. The company typically develops products for years before making official announcements, and timelines for unreleased products can shift based on technical challenges or market conditions.

The late 2027 target suggests Apple is allowing significant development time to address the engineering challenges of fitting computing components, displays, and battery technology into eyeglass frames while maintaining a design that consumers would wear regularly.

cards.headline: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 sets October 23 release date
cards.teaser: The next installment in the Call of Duty franchise launches in October with campaign, multiplayer, and DMZ modes.
cards.body:
Activision announced that Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 will launch on October 23, featuring campaign, multiplayer, and DMZ game modes. The game will be available on PlayStation, and marks the first time the Call of Duty series will release on Nintendo Switch 2.

The developers described the game as offering a more authentic, grounded, and transparent shooter experience. The story imagines a present-day Korean war scenario. The publisher has detailed various game editions and pre-order benefits for players who purchase ahead of the launch date.

cards.headline: MSI releases desktop computer with holographic AI assistant
cards.teaser: The MEG Vision X2 AI+ desktop features a talking holographic display that can adjust RGB lighting and performance settings through voice commands.
cards.body:
MSI has launched the MEG Vision X2 AI+, a gaming desktop featuring an integrated holographic AI assistant called AI Jinni. The system combines traditional computing hardware with a capsule-style holographic display that attaches to the desktop case.

The AI Jinni responds to voice commands to adjust system settings, including RGB lighting configurations and performance parameters, eliminating the need to navigate traditional software menus. This marks MSI's entry into the growing market of AI-enhanced consumer computing devices.

cards.headline: Artist KC Green settles dispute with AI startup over meme use
cards.teaser: The creator of the This is fine meme reached an agreement with Artisan after the startup used the image in advertising.
cards.body:
KC Green, the artist behind the widely shared "This is fine" meme, has reached a settlement with AI startup Artisan over unauthorized use of his work in advertisements. The startup has removed the ads featuring the comic, which depicts a dog sitting calmly in a burning room.

The dispute reflects growing tensions between artists and AI companies over intellectual property rights. Green's case highlights broader concerns about how AI startups use existing creative work without permission or compensation.

cards.headline: Apple plans updated Apple TV and HomePod mini for fall release
cards.teaser: New versions of Apple's streaming box and smart speaker are ready for launch, with a possible Siri Remote redesign also in development.
cards.body:
Apple has prepared updated versions of the Apple TV 4K and HomePod mini for release this fall, according to reports. The company may also refresh the Siri Remote that accompanies the Apple TV.

The updates are reportedly waiting for improvements to Siri before launch. The current Apple TV 4K is approaching a record for the longest period without an update in the product line's history. Apple has not announced timing or specifications for the new devices.

cards.headline: Two major film releases directed by former YouTube creators
cards.teaser: Both of the weekend's top-performing movies were made by directors who built audiences on YouTube before moving to feature films.
cards.body:
The two highest-grossing films released over the weekend were both directed by filmmakers who started their careers creating content for YouTube. The pattern suggests a growing pipeline from online video platforms to theatrical releases.

Multiple directors have transitioned from YouTube to making horror films for traditional studios. The success of this weekend's releases indicates that audiences are responding to projects from creators who built followings through digital platforms.

cards.headline: Black founders raise most quarterly funding since 2022
cards.teaser: Venture capital investment in Black-led startups reached its highest quarterly level in four years, though access challenges persist.
cards.body:
Black startup founders raised their largest amount of quarterly venture capital funding since 2022, marking a recovery from the lower funding levels of recent years, according to Crunchbase data.

Despite the uptick, structural barriers continue to limit opportunities for Black founders. Gené Teare, Crunchbase's head of research, identified access to networks, relationships, and early introductions as key factors affecting which entrepreneurs can secure venture capital and at what funding stages.

hero.headline: Ball State freshman football player dies at 18
hero.body:
The university announced the death of the student-athlete, who had joined the team as a first-year player. Yates-Lyons played the defensive back position for the Cardinals.

Ball State is located in Muncie, Indiana, and competes in the Mid-American Conference. The team had been preparing for the upcoming season when the death occurred.

The circumstances surrounding Yates-Lyons' death were not disclosed by the university. He was in his first year with the program after arriving on campus as part of the most recent recruiting class.

The loss marks a tragedy for the Ball State football program and the wider university community. Yates-Lyons was among the youngest members of the team roster.

College football programs across the country face occasional losses of student-athletes, though deaths of players so young remain rare. The Mid-American Conference includes schools across the Midwest region.

The Cardinals had been conducting offseason workouts and preparations ahead of the fall football season. The defensive back position requires players to cover receivers and provide pass defense.

Ball State football has existed as a program for decades, competing at the NCAA Division I level. The team plays its home games on campus in Muncie.

The university had not released additional information about memorial services or other arrangements. Yates-Lyons had barely begun his college career when his life ended.

Freshman student-athletes typically arrive on campus in summer or fall to begin their collegiate careers. They balance academic requirements with athletic training and competition schedules.

The defensive back position group would have included Yates-Lyons among its members for the upcoming season. His death leaves the team and his family mourning the loss of someone at the very start of adulthood.

cards.headline: Spurs eliminate defending champion Thunder in Game 7
cards.teaser: Victor Wembanyama scored 22 points as San Antonio beat Oklahoma City to reach the NBA Finals.
cards.body:
The San Antonio Spurs defeated the Oklahoma City Thunder 111-103 in Game 7 of the Western Conference finals, advancing to the NBA Finals. Victor Wembanyama was instrumental in the Spurs' victory, leading them past the reigning champions who had dominated much of the regular season.

The win sends San Antonio to face the New York Knicks in the NBA Finals, with Game 1 scheduled for Wednesday in San Antonio. The Thunder's championship defense came to an end against a Spurs team that overcame the odds in this closely contested series.

cards.headline: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander calls MVP season a failure after playoff exit
cards.teaser: The Thunder star won his second consecutive MVP award but said the season fell short after Oklahoma City's elimination.
cards.body:
Shai Gilgeous-Alexander won his second consecutive MVP award, but he expressed disappointment with how the season unfolded. Despite the individual honor, the Oklahoma City Thunder fell short of their championship aspirations, as the team was eliminated from the playoffs before reaching the NBA Finals.

The early exit prevented the Thunder from defending their title from the previous season. For Gilgeous-Alexander, personal accolades could not offset the team's inability to achieve the ultimate goal of winning it all.

cards.headline: Norway wins first world championship medal with overtime upset of Canada
cards.teaser: Norway defeated Canada 3-2 in overtime to capture bronze at the ice hockey world championship.
cards.body:
Norway captured its first ice hockey world championship medal by defeating Canada 3-2 in overtime during the bronze medal game. The stunning upset victory represents a historic breakthrough for the Norwegian national team.

Canada, entering as the favorite, could not contain Norway's push in the extra period, resulting in a loss that kept them off the medal podium at the tournament.

cards.headline: Iga Swiatek knocked out of French Open quarterfinals
cards.teaser: Marta Kostyuk defeated the four-time champion to reach her first French Open quarterfinal.
cards.body:
Marta Kostyuk advanced to the French Open quarterfinals for the first time in her career by defeating four-time champion Iga Swiatek in the fourth round.

The result means all defending singles champions have been eliminated from this year's tournament at Roland Garros, following Coco Gauff's earlier third-round exit to Anastasia Potapova.

cards.headline: Knicks draw nearly half of all NBA Finals bets at New York sportsbook
cards.teaser: DraftKings Sportsbook reported the Knicks have attracted more wagered money than all other teams combined.
cards.body:
The New York Knicks have attracted nearly half of all money wagered on the NBA Finals winner this season at DraftKings Sportsbook in New York. The betting total approaches as much as every other team combined.

The heavy investment in the Knicks reflects strong support from bettors in the New York market. The concentration of wagers on one team represents an unusual betting pattern for the Finals.

cards.headline: South Africa's World Cup arrival delayed by visa problems
cards.teaser: The team's flight to Mexico was rescheduled from Sunday to Monday morning.
cards.body: South Africa's flight to Mexico for the FIFA World Cup opening match has been postponed due to visa issues. The team was originally scheduled to depart from Johannesburg's OR Tambo International Airport and land Sunday morning, but the South African Football Association confirmed the flight has been rebooked for Monday morning instead.

hero.headline: Trump Calls for Cancellation of Freedom 250 Festival After Artist Withdrawals
hero.teaser: Former President Donald Trump urged organizers to cancel a planned festival for America's 250th anniversary after multiple artists withdrew over his involvement.
hero.body:
Former President Donald Trump called for the cancellation of the Freedom 250 concert series after several artists announced they would not perform at the Washington, D.C. event planned for America's 250th anniversary celebrations.

Multiple performers withdrew from the lineup after learning about the organizers' connections to Trump. Martina McBride, Morris Day, Young MC, and members of the band Poison were among those who declined to participate. The artists expressed concerns that the event would take on a political character despite claims from organizers that it would be nonpartisan.

Trump responded to the withdrawals by dismissing the departing performers, calling their music boring. He suggested canceling the festival entirely, later indicating he might host a "Make America Great Again" rally as an alternative event.

The Interior Secretary, Doug Burgum, defended the concert series on CNN's State of the Union program, dismissing criticism of the musicians who opted out. Burgum suggested that some performers had deliberately chosen to segment their audiences by withdrawing from the event. When asked about transparency regarding donors who contributed to the concert series, Burgum declined to commit to publicly identifying them, despite maintaining that the event remained nonpartisan in nature.

Trump's involvement in the festival created tension among performers who wanted to avoid being associated with his political movement. The former president's public criticism of the withdrawing artists and his suggestions about replacing the concert series with a campaign-style rally appeared to confirm the concerns those musicians had raised about the event's political nature.

The Freedom 250 festival was designed as a centerpiece of the nation's 250th anniversary celebrations, intended to feature major entertainment acts performing in the nation's capital. However, the widespread artist departures transformed what organizers had promoted as a patriotic celebration into a controversial event tied directly to Trump's political brand.

The situation highlighted ongoing tensions between entertainment figures and the Trump administration. Some artists have become increasingly cautious about participating in events linked to Trump due to concerns about their public image and political alignment. Others worry that involvement in such events could alienate portions of their fan base.

Trump's response to the cancellations demonstrated his willingness to publicly attack performers who decline to participate in events associated with him. By calling their music boring and suggesting the festival be scrapped altogether, Trump shifted attention from the artists' stated concerns about the event's political character to questions about his temperament and the festival's viability.

The fallout from the Freedom 250 cancellations underscored how Trump's political involvement in cultural events continues to generate significant controversy and resistance from the entertainment community.

cards.headline: Matt Brown, Alaskan Bush People Star, Dies at 42
cards.teaser: Matt Brown, star of the Discovery docudrama series Alaskan Bush People, has died at age 42.
cards.body:
Matt Brown, star of the Discovery docudrama series Alaskan Bush People, has died at age 42. His brother Bear Brown announced the death in a TikTok video posted Saturday night.

Bear Brown said his brother's body was found in a nearby river. He stated that the cause of death looked like suicide, though no official determination has been confirmed.

Matt Brown appeared on Alaskan Bush People, a Discovery series that followed the Brown family living in remote Alaska. The show documented their attempts at self-sufficient living away from modern society.

The series premiered in 2014 and ran for multiple seasons, making the Brown family recognizable figures in reality television. Matt Brown was one of the older siblings featured prominently throughout the show's run.

Bear Brown shared the news directly with followers through social media rather than through official family representatives or the network. The video marked the first public announcement of Matt Brown's death.

The Brown family has faced multiple personal challenges over the years, including the death of family patriarch Billy Brown in 2021. Matt Brown had previously been open about personal struggles during his time on the show.

Discovery has not yet released an official statement about Matt Brown's death. The network had aired Alaskan Bush People for over a decade, building a dedicated audience for the family's story.

Matt Brown's death adds to a difficult period for the Brown family, who have remained in the public eye through their reality television presence. The family relocated from Alaska to Washington state in recent years, where Matt Brown's body was reportedly found.

cards.headline: Ronald LaPread, Co-Founding Bassist of the Commodores, Dies at 75
cards.teaser: Ronald LaPread, a co-founding member and former bassist of the Commodores, has died in Auckland, New Zealand.
cards.body:
Ronald LaPread, who helped establish the Commodores and played bass for the group, died at age 75. He had lived in Auckland, New Zealand for four decades.

The Commodores achieved major success in the 1970s and 1980s with hits including "Brick House," "Easy," and "Three Times a Lady." LaPread was among the founding members who formed the group while attending college.

cards.headline: Dua Lipa Marries Callum Turner in London Ceremony
cards.teaser: Pop singer Dua Lipa married actor Callum Turner during an intimate ceremony at a historic London venue.
cards.body:
Dua Lipa and Callum Turner were married at Old Marylebone Town Hall in London. The wedding took place during an intimate ceremony attended by close family and friends.

Old Marylebone Town Hall is a historic venue in central London that has hosted numerous celebrity weddings over the decades. The couple had kept their relationship relatively private before the wedding announcement.

cards.headline: Jay-Z Performs at Roots Picnic in Philadelphia
cards.teaser: Jay-Z headlined the 2026 Roots Picnic in Philadelphia, drawing thousands to Fairmount Park for the annual music festival.
cards.body:
Jay-Z headlined this year's Roots Picnic at Belmont Plateau in Philadelphia's Fairmount Park. The performance featured a freestyle that included references to Kanye West, Drake, and Nicki Minaj.

The 2026 edition of the Roots Picnic featured the largest lineup in the festival's history. Jay-Z also performed a secret concert in Philadelphia ahead of the main festival event, according to local reports.

cards.headline: WWE Hosts Clash in Italy Event
cards.teaser: WWE held its Clash in Italy premium live event, featuring championship matches including Cody Rhodes versus Gunther and Roman Reigns versus Jacob Fatu.
cards.body:
WWE's Clash in Italy 2026 took place with several high-profile matches on the card. The event featured Cody Rhodes facing Gunther and Roman Reigns taking on Jacob Fatu.

The event was broadcast as a livestream for viewers around the world. Multiple wrestling media outlets provided live coverage and analysis of the matches throughout the show.

cards.headline: KSI Leaves Sidemen After 13 Years
cards.teaser: British YouTuber KSI has departed the Sidemen collective after being part of the group since its formation in 2013.
cards.body:
KSI, whose real name is Olajide Olatunji, announced his departure from the Sidemen YouTube group. He had been a member of the collective since it was formed in 2013.

The Sidemen became one of the most successful YouTube groups in Britain, known for collaborative videos and charity football matches. KSI has built a separate career in music and boxing while maintaining his role in the group.

hero.headline: White House predicts Strait of Hormuz reopening within two months
hero.body:
National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett said oil shipments could resume through the Strait of Hormuz within one to two months, after the waterway closed during the U.S.-Israeli conflict in Iran.

Hassett told ABC's Jonathan Karl that more traffic is passing through the strait than previously reported. The strait has been a focal point of the conflict, which began three months ago.

The closure has disrupted global oil flows through one of the world's most important shipping routes. Iran has used cheap drones to close the strait, according to Sen. Chris Coons, a Delaware Democrat who said Iran has grown stronger since the war began.

Coons claimed Iran's position improved over the past 90 days because of its use of drones in the strait. The waterway connects the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and handles a significant portion of global oil shipments.

Hassett's timeline suggests the administration expects progress in reopening the shipping lane despite ongoing military operations. The conflict between the United States, Israel, and Iran has now stretched into its fourth month.

The economic impact of the closure has affected global energy markets, though Hassett provided no details about specific measures being taken to reopen the strait. His prediction indicates the White House believes the current situation will improve in the coming weeks.

The strait's closure marks one of the most significant economic consequences of the conflict. Reopening it would restore normal oil traffic patterns and reduce pressure on global energy supplies.

Hassett made his comments during a television interview focused on economic policy and the administration's response to the ongoing conflict. He did not elaborate on what conditions would need to change for shipping to resume or whether negotiations are underway to secure the waterway.

cards.headline: Senator says Iran stronger after three months of war
cards.teaser: A Delaware Democrat claims Iran has gained strength since the U.S. conflict began, using drones to control the Strait of Hormuz.
cards.body:
Sen. Chris Coons said Iran has strengthened its strategic position during the three-month conflict with the U.S. The Delaware Democrat pointed to Iran's use of inexpensive drones to blockade the Strait of Hormuz as evidence, noting the waterway remains closed to shipping.

The war has coincided with surging inflation in the U.S., with energy prices rising at their fastest pace in three years as of April. Household incomes have declined for three consecutive months after adjusting for inflation, fueling public frustration with the administration's economic management ahead of midterm elections.

cards.headline: Pence opposes Justice Department anti-weaponization fund
cards.teaser: The former vice president called the DOJ fund a bad idea and urged the Trump administration to eliminate it.
cards.body:
Former Vice President Mike Pence criticized the Department of Justice's "anti-weaponization" fund, calling it "a bad idea" and urging officials to eliminate the program entirely.

The fund has drawn scrutiny beyond Pence's comments. A federal judge in Miami has reopened Donald Trump's $10 billion lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service, examining whether a $1.8 billion settlement related to the fund represents collusion or fraud. The judge is investigating claims that the settlement itself may be fraudulent.

cards.headline: Jill Biden says former president was slowing down in office
cards.teaser: The former first lady said Joe Biden showed signs of slowing down before he dropped his 2024 presidential bid.
cards.body:
Former first lady Jill Biden said her husband was slowing down during his presidency, according to her first interview since leaving the White House. She told CBS News correspondent Rita Braver that she never saw signs of cognitive or mental issues.

Jill Biden made the comments in an interview released on a Sunday news program. She discussed the period before Joe Biden dropped his 2024 presidential campaign.

cards.headline: Kentucky governor says Texas Senate race competitive after Paxton runoff win
cards.teaser: Andy Beshear said Democrats have a chance to win a Texas Senate seat after Ken Paxton secured the Republican nomination.
cards.body:
Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear said Democrats have an opportunity to win a Texas Senate seat following state Attorney General Ken Paxton's recent runoff victory. Beshear suggested that Texas is now competitive for Democrats in the upcoming general election.

Paxton will face off against his Democratic opponent after securing the Republican nomination. Democrats have not won a statewide Senate race in Texas in more than three decades, making Beshear's assessment notable as he signals potential Democratic gains in the traditionally Republican state.

cards.headline: Zelensky hopes Trump envoy and Kushner will visit Kyiv
cards.teaser: The Ukrainian president said he wants White House special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to come for talks in the coming weeks.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky expressed hope that White House special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will travel to Kyiv for discussions. Speaking to CBS News host Margaret Brennan, Zelensky indicated he wants these meetings to take place in the coming weeks.

The Ukrainian leader was asked whether he had been in contact with the envoys and Secretary of State Marco Rubio, signaling Kyiv's interest in direct engagement with Trump's diplomatic team.

cards.headline: Republican National Committee plans midterm convention before election
cards.teaser: RNC Chairman Joe Gruters said the party will hold a convention between the last primary and the general election.
cards.body:
Republican National Committee Chairman Joe Gruters said the party will hold a midterm convention before the general election, following a plan President Trump outlined last September. Gruters said there is a short window between the final primary ballots and the general election.

The RNC is moving forward with the convention plans despite the compressed timeline. Trump proposed the midterm convention concept nine months ago.
